bull_bear.body:
- Landmark, well-recognised owned brand — Hotel The Suryaa is described as a prominent landmark hotel among the star hotels in Delhi, with a new and fresh look
- Prime South Delhi micro-location, about a 20-minute drive from Connaught Place and 40 minutes from the domestic airport
- Balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with diversified brand architecture across geographies and segments
- Stable stream of fee-based income supporting sustained growth
- Occupancy improved to 86.31% in FY2025-26 from 85.60% in FY2024-25, with ARR rising to Rs 8,808 from Rs 8,273, indicating pricing power
- Healthy balance sheet and strong liquidity maintained despite a dynamic operating environment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Corporate guarantee on the subsidiary's EXIM Bank loan — the auditor's Emphasis of Matter — The auditors draw attention to note 26: the loan from EXIM Bank availed by CHL International, a subsidiary for which the Company is a guarantor, is a matter of litigation, with cases filed by EXIM Bank against the Company pending adjudication in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Debt Recovery Tribunal, Delhi. This is an off-balance-sheet exposure crystallised on the parent, not on the operating hotel.
- One Time Settlement of USD 34 million still only 'under implementation' — EXIM Bank, the Principal Borrower and the Guarantors entered into a One Time Settlement for an amount of USD 34 million (EXIM Bank approval letter dated 23.11.2023), and the Economic Court of Dushanbe crystalized the liability against the borrowers/guarantors at USD 34 million by judgement dated 12.12.2023 in Case No. 52/2023. The OTS was still under implementation as on the balance sheet date, so the exposure is not extinguished and non-performance would revive the full claim.
- Parallel personal and corporate guarantee proceedings before DRT-III — EXIM Bank has filed separate applications in pending Original Applications — Transfer Application No. 221 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs Dr. Lalit Kumar Malhotra) and Transfer Application No. 224 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs CHL Limited) — before Debt Recovery Tribunal-III against the personal and corporate guarantors, meaning the litigation runs on multiple fora simultaneously and ties promoter-family personal guarantees to the Company's.
- Management states no material risks were identified, despite the auditor's Emphasis of Matter — The MD&A 'Risk and concerns' section says that based on the assessment carried out during the year, no material or significant risks have been identified that are likely to adversely affect the business, operations or financial performance. That assertion sits alongside an unresolved guarantee litigation flagged by the statutory auditors, so the disclosed risk framework understates the actual exposure and gives an investor little visibility into risk monitoring.
- Single-asset, single-city concentration — The entire operating narrative rests on one property, Hotel The Suryaa in New Friends Colony, South Delhi. Revenue, occupancy and ARR all depend on one micro-market, one asset's condition and one city's demand cycle; any localised disruption, regulatory action or refurbishment shutdown has no offsetting property.
- Litigated statutory liabilities can hit earnings in lumps — The MD&A states that while revenue remained broadly stable, profitability was impacted due to the payment of a long-pending Property Tax litigation liability, which was settled and paid during the year. A single legacy municipal-tax settlement was large enough to move reported profitability materially, showing that unresolved statutory disputes are a real earnings risk for a company of this size.
- Geopolitical disruption to travel flows — The MD&A threats discussion flags the Middle East conflict, which has disrupted airspace, reduced travel flows to the region and affected destinations relying on the Middle East as a key global transit hub handling around 14% of all international passengers. For a Delhi hotel dependent on international and corporate arrivals, a hit to connectivity and traveller confidence feeds directly into occupancy and rate.
- Forward-looking exposure to macro, policy and regulatory change — The cautionary statement enumerates the risk factors the Company itself names: changes in economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments and industry trends, all beyond its control, with actual results potentially differing materially from stated expectations.

outlook.body:
- Operate a balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with a diversified brand architecture across geographies and segments, backed by a stable stream of fee-based income, as the platform for sustained growth
- Strengthen operational capabilities and pursue operational excellence at the hotel, while maintaining prudent financial management and robust corporate governance
- Sustain pricing momentum on ARR alongside high occupancy — ARR rose to Rs 8,808 in FY2025-26 from Rs 8,273, with occupancy at 86.31% versus 85.60%

- Attract, develop and retain talent through structured recruitment, continuous learning and skill-enhancement programmes, and maintain harmonious industrial relations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no capex project, capacity addition, new property, commissioning or ramp-up timeline. The only asset-level detail is the existing footprint of the single owned hotel, Hotel The Suryaa in New Friends Colony, South Delhi, described as having a new and fresh look up among the star hotels in Delhi, with its existing room inventory and F&B outlets (Sampan, Ssence, Atrium Lounge Bar) and the Club One wellness and fitness centre. The Company describes a balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties and a stable stream of fee-based income as a platform for sustained growth, but names no specific expansion project. The 'Capital commitments' named-disclosure block reached this bundle as headings only ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, net of advances') with no figure attached, so no rupee quantum is stated.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the hospitality sector to remain stable in FY2026-27, supported by domestic leisure travel and MICE demand, with room rates likely to remain firm
- ICRA projects industry revenues to grow ~7-9% Y-o-Y in FY2026-27, with occupancy and ARR continuing to improve
- Resilient leisure demand and improving corporate travel supported occupancy during the year, while continued supply discipline helped sustain pricing momentum across ADR and RevPAR
- A structural demand-supply imbalance across key markets, coupled with improving infrastructure, may support sustained occupancy and healthy pricing, including in select Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets
- Sector-level base is strong: national occupancy stood at 64% in 2025 (2024: 63.0%), ADR at Rs 8,624 (+8.5% Y-o-Y) and RevPAR at Rs 5,522 (+8.7% Y-o-Y) per Horwath HTL
- Domestic tourism remains the primary growth driver, with domestic visitor spending projected by WTTC to reach INR 19.0 trillion in 2026 (+7.5%) and INR 36.5 trillion by 2036 (6.8% CAGR)
- Near-term risk: geopolitical developments in West Asia and related aviation disruptions could temporarily impact select international and corporate travel corridors while keeping fuel, logistics and utility costs elevated
- The Middle East conflict has disrupted airspace and reduced travel flows to a region handling around 14% of all international passengers, a headwind management flags for 2026

- Sustain pricing momentum on ARR alongside high occupancy — ARR rose to Rs 8,808 in FY2025-26 from Rs 8,273, with occupancy at 86.31% versus 85.60%
- Maintain a healthy balance sheet and strong liquidity; the long-pending Property Tax litigation liability was settled and paid during the year, clearing a legacy overhang
- Attract, develop and retain talent through structured recruitment, continuous learning and skill-enhancement programmes, and maintain harmonious industrial relations

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections disclose no capex project, capacity addition, new property, commissioning or ramp-up timeline. The only asset-level detail is the existing footprint of the single owned hotel, Hotel The Suryaa in New Friends Colony, South Delhi, described as having a new and fresh look up among the star hotels in Delhi, with its existing room inventory and F&B outlets (Sampan, Ssence, Atrium Lounge Bar) and the Club One wellness and fitness centre. The Company describes a balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties and a stable stream of fee-based income as a platform for sustained growth, but names no specific expansion project. The 'Capital commitments' named-disclosure block reached this bundle as headings only ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account, net of advances') with no figure attached, so no rupee quantum is stated.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Landmark, well-recognised owned brand — Hotel The Suryaa is described as a prominent landmark hotel among the star hotels in Delhi, with a new and fresh look
- Prime South Delhi micro-location, about a 20-minute drive from Connaught Place and 40 minutes from the domestic airport
- Balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with diversified brand architecture across geographies and segments
- Stable stream of fee-based income supporting sustained growth
- Occupancy improved to 86.31% in FY2025-26 from 85.60% in FY2024-25, with ARR rising to Rs 8,808 from Rs 8,273, indicating pricing power
- Healthy balance sheet and strong liquidity maintained despite a dynamic operating environment

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Corporate guarantee on the subsidiary's EXIM Bank loan — the auditor's Emphasis of Matter — The auditors draw attention to note 26: the loan from EXIM Bank availed by CHL International, a subsidiary for which the Company is a guarantor, is a matter of litigation, with cases filed by EXIM Bank against the Company pending adjudication in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Debt Recovery Tribunal, Delhi. This is an off-balance-sheet exposure crystallised on the parent, not on the operating hotel.
- One Time Settlement of USD 34 million still only 'under implementation' — EXIM Bank, the Principal Borrower and the Guarantors entered into a One Time Settlement for an amount of USD 34 million (EXIM Bank approval letter dated 23.11.2023), and the Economic Court of Dushanbe crystalized the liability against the borrowers/guarantors at USD 34 million by judgement dated 12.12.2023 in Case No. 52/2023. The OTS was still under implementation as on the balance sheet date, so the exposure is not extinguished and non-performance would revive the full claim.
- Parallel personal and corporate guarantee proceedings before DRT-III — EXIM Bank has filed separate applications in pending Original Applications — Transfer Application No. 221 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs Dr. Lalit Kumar Malhotra) and Transfer Application No. 224 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs CHL Limited) — before Debt Recovery Tribunal-III against the personal and corporate guarantors, meaning the litigation runs on multiple fora simultaneously and ties promoter-family personal guarantees to the Company's.
- Management states no material risks were identified, despite the auditor's Emphasis of Matter — The MD&A 'Risk and concerns' section says that based on the assessment carried out during the year, no material or significant risks have been identified that are likely to adversely affect the business, operations or financial performance. That assertion sits alongside an unresolved guarantee litigation flagged by the statutory auditors, so the disclosed risk framework understates the actual exposure and gives an investor little visibility into risk monitoring.
- Single-asset, single-city concentration — The entire operating narrative rests on one property, Hotel The Suryaa in New Friends Colony, South Delhi. Revenue, occupancy and ARR all depend on one micro-market, one asset's condition and one city's demand cycle; any localised disruption, regulatory action or refurbishment shutdown has no offsetting property.
- Litigated statutory liabilities can hit earnings in lumps — The MD&A states that while revenue remained broadly stable, profitability was impacted due to the payment of a long-pending Property Tax litigation liability, which was settled and paid during the year. A single legacy municipal-tax settlement was large enough to move reported profitability materially, showing that unresolved statutory disputes are a real earnings risk for a company of this size.
- Geopolitical disruption to travel flows — The MD&A threats discussion flags the Middle East conflict, which has disrupted airspace, reduced travel flows to the region and affected destinations relying on the Middle East as a key global transit hub handling around 14% of all international passengers. For a Delhi hotel dependent on international and corporate arrivals, a hit to connectivity and traveller confidence feeds directly into occupancy and rate.
- Forward-looking exposure to macro, policy and regulatory change — The cautionary statement enumerates the risk factors the Company itself names: changes in economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments and industry trends, all beyond its control, with actual results potentially differing materially from stated expectations.
